assembly_notes:
Identity: a graduated plate carrying N swing arms on one shared +Z pivot, plus exactly one locking fastener on that same axis. EVERY joint in this category is revolute about (0,0,1) — there is no prismatic, continuous or non-vertical joint anywhere in the 9-record pool, which is what makes the category machine-checkable.

core_domain = 5 body_form x 4 arm_form x 4 lock_module = 80, all of which must build. raw_domain = 80 x 5 N values = 400. Graduation tick counts, palette and blade proportions count toward neither.

Two cross-slot risks, both resolved by derivation rather than by gating:
(a) The pool contains TWO different arm bearings. 001 and 002 build an annular thrust boss and seat the arm's flat underside on it (gap asserted 0..0.00005); 003 builds no boss and gives the arm a real 0.15 mm running clearance (asserted 0.00002..0.00025). `arm_seat_z_m` branches on `body_bearing_kind` so a 003-family plate combined with any arm still produces the source's clearance instead of a fabricated contact.
(b) `quadrant_sector` re-derives the arm's joint limits from the plate's angular span, and the graduation count with it. A 90 deg plate under a 180 deg sweep would swing the blade off the scale. This is the only true cross-slot binding in the category and it gets a named corner.

Construction rule taken from the source pool: graduations are CUT into (001 L66-L86) or welded into (002 L72-L134) a single CAD solid. Record 003 instead emits 108 separate Box visuals for its ticks, and because sdk/_core/v0/exact_collisions.py derives one collision per visual 1:1, that route turns a decorative scale into ~116 collision bodies. The rebuild uses the 001/002 route for every candidate including the two forked from 003. Same visible detail, one visual per part.

Part tree: plate (root) -> N arms in parallel -> lock. The lock's parent is the plate for knurled_clamp_screw and the topmost arm for the other three; that is source-attested per candidate (001 L259-L260 vs 002 L307 and 003 L275), not a free choice. Seeds carry N+2 parts and N+1 joints.

No allowances are needed anywhere: not one of the 9 records calls allow_overlap or allow_isolated_part. Every moving member has a real seated or clearance-fitted contact, and the bores are genuinely cut, so the fastener shaft passes through the plate without intersecting it.

Multiplicity arm_count rationale (moved here when the malformed multiplicity keys were repaired):
N arms share one pivot axis and stack in Z. The rule is taken verbatim from var_arm_count_dual_arms L211-L246 and is ALREADY INDEX-GENERAL THERE: arm_z[i] = arm_seat_z_m + i * arm_thickness_m, every arm parented to the PLATE (never chained arm-to-arm), and the lock lifted to clamp_z = arm_z[N-1] + arm_thickness_m (L284). Rest angles are spread evenly across the plate's angular span rather than the source's hard-coded [48 deg, 120 deg], which is the same intent generalised.

The range is bounded by HOST CAPACITY and BUDGET, not by which integers the source pool happens to contain. The pool builds N=1 and N=2; those are evidence that the stacking rule holds, not an upper bound. Upper bound 5 comes from two real constraints: (a) host capacity - the stack must stay under the fastener's grip, expressed as arm_stack_height_m <= body_radius_m * 0.6, which at the thinnest plate/thickest arm corner is what actually binds; and (b) budget - at N=5 a seed carries 7 parts and 6 revolute joints, against a measured fleet maximum of 33 parts / 32 joints and a 120 s preflight soft budget, so 5 is comfortably inside the envelope. Lower bound 1 is the single-arm object, which is what 8 of the 9 records build.

Anchor repair (authoring stage, before the first preflight pass): the single protractor_pivot_lock_identity anchor demanded parent_role 'top_swing_arm' for all four lock candidates. That is unsatisfiable twice over: (a) knurled_clamp_screw is source-attested as PLATE-parented (001 L259-L260), which is exactly what the lock_joint_parent_role derivation encodes, and (b) no part can carry role 'top_swing_arm' while protractor_swing_arm_identity also requires role 'swing_arm' to count arm_count. The anchor is therefore split by joint parent: protractor_pivot_lock_identity keeps the three arm-parented candidates with parent_role 'swing_arm', and protractor_plate_parented_lock_identity covers knurled_clamp_screw with parent_role 'graduated_plate'. Required roles and required_author_checks are unchanged.

derived.name: body_top_z_m
derived.rationale: Top of the plate's own material, including the raised scale rim where the 003 family builds one.

derived.expression: body_top_z_m + (pivot_boss_h_m if body_bearing_kind == 'thrust_boss' else arm_running_gap_m + arm_thickness_m * 0.5)
derived.name: arm_seat_z_m
derived.rationale: THE central derivation of the category, and it has two branches because the pool has two bearings (SourceMap mating rule 1). Thrust-boss bodies (001, 002) put the arm's flat underside exactly on the boss top, so the seat offset IS the boss height and the author gap check is 0..0.00005. The 003 family builds no boss at all and the arm rides a real 0.15 mm air gap, so the seat is the gap plus the arm's own half thickness because that arm is extruded symmetrically about its origin. Closing the 003 gap to satisfy a support check would be a source-fidelity regression.

derived.name: body_bearing_kind
derived.rationale: Which bearing the plate candidate builds. Carried as a derived value so the arm and the lock both read one source of truth.

derived.name: arm_hub_top_z_m
derived.rationale: Top of the topmost arm's material in its own frame. double_ended_blade carries its own boss (003 L70-L76) because its body side has none.

derived.expression: sector_span_rad if body_form == 'quadrant_sector' else (2.0 * pi if body_form in ('full_circle_annulus', 'full_circle_solid_plate') else pi)
derived.name: body_angular_span_rad
derived.rationale: Angular span of graduated plate material.

derived.name: arm_swing_lower_rad
derived.rationale: Lower joint limit of every arm pivot.

derived.name: arm_swing_upper_rad
derived.rationale: THE cross-slot binding of this category. var_body_form_quadrant L245-L253 changes the arm joint from (-pi, +pi) to (0, pi/2) purely because the plate became a 90 deg sector, and its author test L370-L384 asserts it. An arm that sweeps past the end of the graduations is not measuring anything. Same record also re-derives the tick counts from the same span (L158, L180).

derived.name: outer_tick_count
derived.rationale: 5-degree graduations across the real span. 37 at 180 deg (001 L66, 002 L83), 19 at 90 deg (quadrant L158), 72 at 360 deg (003 L129).

derived.name: arm_stack_height_m
derived.rationale: Total Z occupied by the arm stack, from var_arm_count_dual_arms L211-L215.

derived.name: top_arm_z_m
derived.rationale: Frame origin of the topmost arm; arms below it are face-stacked at one thickness pitch.

derived.name: lock_seat_z_m
derived.rationale: Seating plane of the fastener. Source 001 L261 authors 0.0041 = 0.0024 seat + 0.0017 arm thickness, and var_arm_count_dual_arms L284 generalises it to arm_z[-1] + arm_thickness. 002 and 003 use Origin() so the lock frame IS the arm frame and the head is extruded off the arm's top face.

derived.name: lock_shaft_r_m
derived.rationale: SourceMap mating rule 2: shaft_r = min(bore_r) - 0.7..1.2 mm, measured across all three origins (001 1.2 mm, 002 0.7 mm, 003 0.9 mm), and asserted as an author check in 003 L430-L437. This is why the shaft can pass through two real bores without a solid intersection — the clearance is geometric, not an allowance.

derived.name: lock_seat_r_m
derived.rationale: Radius of the fastener's seating face, bounded by the hub it lands on. 002 and the cam lever both assert expect_within(lock, arm, axes='xy', margin=0.0002).

derived.name: retainer_top_z_m
derived.rationale: capstan_screw_retainer only. The retainer's top face must land on the plate underside at world z=0, which in the lock's own frame is -lock_seat_z_m. Source 003: retainer centre -0.00365, length 0.0009 -> top -0.0032 = -ARM_FRAME_Z exactly.

derived.name: hub_relief_required
derived.rationale: Host adaptation gate. The cam lever needs a flat relief cut into the arm hub top for its handle (var_lock_cam_lever L158-L164). Without it the handle would rest on air.

derived.name: lock_joint_parent_role
derived.rationale: Which part carries the lock joint. Source-attested per candidate, not free choice.
